findings.evidence: “Triggered by … passing document path(s)” is broader than the task, and “needs review-and-fix” does not clearly invite review-only requests. The description does not distinguish reviewing an existing plan from writing or executing one.
findings.fix: Use when asked to review an existing design, requirements document, RFC, spec, or implementation plan before the next step, even if the request is just “is this ready to build?” Dispatches independent reviewers, checks the document against its lifecycle stage and worktree, and reports findings. When revisions are authorized, routes fixes through the owning framework or a generic fixer and re-reviews up to the iteration cap. Supports Superpowers, GSD, OpenSpec, Spec Kit, Kiro, BMAD, and generic documents; use --cross-ai or --no-cross-ai to control reviewer dispatch. Not for writing a new spec or plan, executing a plan, reviewing a code diff, or setting up reviewers.

findings.evidence: “Resolve CODEBASE_ROOT from the document's own worktree … never from your CWD. Use git worktree list when unsure.” The table repeats both the instruction and the phantom-findings rationale already given in Step 0.1.
findings.fix: Keep the full decision rule and rationale in Step 0.1. Make the Hard rules row a short pointer to that step and record the consolidation; preserve the worktree check and its rationale.

findings.evidence: The main file is 556 lines. The always-loaded “Lane capability block, lenses and refusals” section includes the full role and lens-note tables plus the owner-only after-approval command, none of which an ordinary review needs to consult in full.
findings.fix: Keep the pre-spawn refusal and no-automatic-edit rules in SKILL.md. Move the role, lens-note, and capability field details to the existing Lane capabilities section of references/cross-ai-dispatch.md, and move the owner-only command and accept/reject details to references/edit-lens-pass.md. Link to the latter only when the owner asks for the pass or needs to interpret its result.

findings.evidence: “Remove $RUN_TMP_DIR (rm -rf …) only when … Approved” gates deletion on outcome but not on directory ownership. The resume branch obtains the directory from a pointer rather than creating it in the current invocation.
findings.fix: Bind cleanup to the canonical run directory recorded when this skill created it. On resume, require that the pointer resolve to that recorded directory under the expected temp root; if ownership or identity cannot be verified, retain it and tell the user why.

findings.evidence: The prompt says “the primary lane's dispatch-reviewer call exits 65,” but the only lane in the supplied fixture uses a placeholder OpenCode model. No fake runner or model inventory produces the stipulated exit or stderr record, so the setup can skip the lane before exercising the assertion.
findings.fix: Supply a deterministic fake runner and matching model inventory. Have the fixture emit the refusal record and exit 65 from the actual dispatch path, then assert that the record is quoted and that neither a retry nor another reviewer is launched.

findings.evidence: “When the slash command succeeds, dispatches gsd-plan-checker” has no runnable success setup: the supplied phase has no REVIEWS.md, which the current route requires before invoking the planner.
findings.fix: Split the GSD case into a missing-REVIEWS.md fixture that asserts handoff without invocation and a fixture with owner-approved, matching REVIEWS.md and a fake invocable planner and validator that asserts validation precedes re-review.

findings.evidence: “Handle the direct-edit ones via 3a and the native one via the appropriate 3b variant” promises split routing, but both prompts receive the full document list and full report. For a fused document with one direct-edit finding and one native-owned finding, the generic fixer is told to treat both findings as its contract.
findings.fix: Bind each finding to its document and archetype before routing. Give each handler a report containing only its assigned findings and only the necessary document paths. If a finding cannot be routed unambiguously, surface it rather than handing it to both writers.

findings.evidence: The fixer status table ends with “No Status line” and omits the sibling fixer's documented “Failure — <reason>” status. A document removed after review can produce a valid fixer response for which the orchestrator has no action.
findings.fix: Add a Failure row that stops the loop, preserves the report, and quotes the fixer's reason. Treat any other unrecognized fixer status as a failure rather than continuing.

findings.evidence: The stage-gap output says “Reviewed <existing> as <archetype>,” but Step 0.6 stops before dispatch and only offers to review the existing document. Following the template falsely claims a review occurred.
findings.fix: Use “I can review <existing> as <archetype> now, or wait until <next stage> is produced.” Do not claim a review or dispatch a substitute without the user's choice.

findings.evidence: The verbatim dispatch snippet inserts an unquoted <CODEBASE_ROOT> and a free-form --files list. A checkout or plan path containing spaces becomes multiple shell arguments instead of one path. The resume argv example repeats the same problem.
findings.fix: Construct argument arrays and pass each resolved path as one quoted argument, including the root, in the timeout, dispatch, and resume examples. Show one example with spaces in both the checkout path and the document name.

findings.evidence: “Schedule one one-shot re-invoke … rounded up to the next whole minute” does not guarantee the requested minimum delay on Claude Code. Its official scheduler documentation says one-shots on :00 or :30 can run up to 90 seconds early.
findings.fix: Record the absolute retry-not-before time, select a supported minute at or after it that avoids :00 and :30, and check the deadline again before executing the saved argv. Cite https://code.claude.com/docs/en/scheduled-tasks.md#when-a-one-shot-task-runs-early with the verification date; if the host cannot honor the delay, print the resume pointer for the owner.
